summary: D16 (the at_hard_ceiling overshoot) is implemented as CLAMP, under the reading the mechanism supports, with the clamp made visible. capacity/api.py::_clamped_lift is the one spelling of min(derive.lift_to(...), hard) -- guarded with a max so it can never LOWER a cap, which is not decoration: a restored cap of 5000 against FAB_SLOTS=4096 is reachable and a bare min would take 904 slots off it. I took reading (ii), the per-lift arithmetic with NO state, and recorded it in observe's docstring with the three facts that rule out reading (i) and the report line that tells them apart. Visibility: two counters seeded on the Valve ledger (cap.lifts_clamped_experts / _vocab), Decision.clamped for the one flush, and a new Gate cap.clamp built by capacity/api.py::_clamp_gate, whose FOUR states I printed from real builds. The false equation the ruling exposed is gone: over a 10368-cell lever sweep, printed one-lift arithmetics ABOVE the ceiling went 7644 -> 0, and NO cap.valve or cap.vocab_arm_honest verdict moved on any cell. In levers.py I REFUTED the filed stale-carrier item (it was already corrected), made the budget figures K13-parseable (1 numeric claim examined -> 7, each of the four numbers corruption-proved), and removed three false universals about negative levers and CAP_LIFT=2.0 that api.py had corrected in its own copy while this carrier kept them. docs/04_CONTRACT.md needs the ruling and carries one of the same false universals; it is not mine and NO check fails until it lands -- both items are in unfinished with exact text.

findings.detail: D16 IMPLEMENTED, AND THE INTERPRETATION IS ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN IMPLIED. observe's docstring now states the ruling ('let's soft clamp if a ceiling is overshot, until it goes down'), the arithmetic it applies (capacity/api.py::_clamped_lift, replacing the bare derive.lift_to the docstring used to name), and WHICH READING OF 'until it goes down' this is. I TOOK READING (ii) -- a per-lift arithmetic operation with NO state -- and the mechanism, not a preference, decides it. THREE FACTS RULE OUT (i), each sufficient alone. (1) A cap may never be lowered: the module's founding sentence is 'raised, by a little, never lowered', new_valve refuses CAP_LIFT<0 / CAP_LIFT_MIN<0 at startup to hold it, and 'released' in (i) means the soft cap moves DOWN off the ceiling -- so (i) is not a reading of this valve, it is a different mechanism. (2) Nothing persists a clamped state: Valve declares fourteen fields and none is a clamp flag, and CAP.state's declared payload is 'the lifted caps AND the two pin clocks AND the high-water marks' and nothing else -- a state with an exit that evaporates at the next checkpoint is the M38 family arriving through the repair for a different one. (3) The signal (i) would release on does not reach observe as a LEVEL: what arrives per flush is live_experts/live_vocab against the caps (a boolean per arm) and improving, and the hard ceiling is FROZEN onto the Valve at build. HOW THE OWNER TELLS THEM APART, which is in the docstring: under (ii) an arm reaches the ceiling ONCE and stays, so cap.clamp shows at most one clamped lift per arm and every later flush is at_hard_ceiling; under (i) the cap would LEAVE the ceiling when the population fell and be lifted back, so lifts_experts would keep climbing and the reported cap would print a SMALLER number than on an earlier flush. A cap that ever goes down is (i), and on this implementation it is a defect. THE COMPOSITION WITH THE NEIGHBOURS IS WRITTEN DOWN: at_hard_ceiling is UNCHANGED (cap >= hard, evaluated BEFORE the lift -- the reading new_valve's gate reasons already spelled), which is why the clamp can bite only once per arm and why the closed block-reason set does NOT grow; dead_rows_unmasked is a refusal for dishonesty and not a clamp; and derive.lift_to returning the cap unchanged when both terms round to zero is a third not-moving case with a third reading (cap.valve's UNREACHABLE). Also recorded: a clamped lift does NOT enter the block-reason histogram, because that histogram counts flushes on which NO lift happened.

findings.detail: ONE SPELLING OF THE CLAMP, module-level and private, so it changes no entry-point count (entry_points stays 132, stubs 83, implemented 49 by K13's own AST reader). It is max(int(cap), min(derive.lift_to(cap, frac, floor), int(hard))). THE max IS A GUARD ON A REACHABLE INPUT AND NOT AN UNTRIPPABLE ONE, which is the objection this tree makes to decoration: min() alone RAISES only from below the ceiling, and from a cap already at or above it the min IS the ceiling and the cap comes DOWN -- the C30 inversion arriving through the repair for a different one. Two reachable inputs exercise it: CAP_FAB_START=5000 against FAB_SLOTS=4096 (operator), and a checkpoint restoring a lifted cap above a ceiling a later run lowered. observe never reaches that state because at_hard_ceiling refuses cap >= hard first, but the refusal is a caller's discipline and this is where the arithmetic lives -- the same argument Caps.headroom is built on. Three callers now share it: observe (declared), new_valve's _lift_moves, and new_valve's printed arithmetic.

findings.detail: THE CLAMP IS VISIBLE, IN FOUR STATES OUT OF A RECORD THAT HAS THREE VERDICTS. The counters cap.lifts_clamped_experts and cap.lifts_clamped_vocab are SEEDED AT 0 in new_valve's ledger -- the precedent is cap.mask_dead_rows, frozen on there because observe reads no wires of its own -- so the ledger new_valve seeds goes from EIGHT keys to TEN and the RECORD TYPES block says so (K11 resolves provenance tokens against that block). Decision gains `clamped` for the one flush. Gate cap.clamp is built by _clamp_gate, called at startup by new_valve and DECLARED to be rebuilt from the live ledger by CAP.counters, so the two lines cannot disagree; value is '<clamped> clamped of <lifts> lift(s) taken' on every arm, which is what tells the two middle states apart -- Gate.line prints (value vs threshold) for exactly that. THE FOURTH STATE IS NOT SMUGGLED INTO A VERDICT: UNREACHABLE = no lift can be earned at all (it shares cap.valve's reachability precondition and its `dead` sentences, because a clamp is a property of a lift); armed with 0 of 0 = no lift was earned; armed with 0 of N = every earned lift applied IN FULL; FIRED = M of N were CLAMPED. The docstring maps this onto D16's table explicitly, because D16's 'fired' column is about THE LIFT and this gate's FIRED is about THE CLAMP, and reading one onto the other would say a clamped lift is an ordinary one.

findings.detail: THE CLAUSE READ '... which observe refuses by name as at_hard_ceiling, and one earned lift takes it to 4423, which is not below the ceiling either'. Every equation in it is true, and under the clamp ruling the SENTENCE is not: no lift is taken there at all, because at_hard_ceiling is evaluated before the lift is computed, so 'one earned lift takes it to' names an action the mechanism does not perform.
